digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow and test infrastructure
propositions: Ubuntu CI jobs occupy 30+ runner-minutes per Verified run with individual test phases exceeding 30 seconds, contributing to org-wide runner queue contention and delaying completion past the 20-30 minute target.

Bridge cadence test calls _bridge_schedule() 1,440 times inside a comprehension, forcing repeated YAML parsing (7.653s per parse) instead of once, wasting ~342 seconds per Verified run on I/O rather than exhaustive arithmetic.

Pandoc corpus tests execute all 232 eligible units and 884 hardening units through real Pandoc subprocesses repeatedly but assert only cardinality witnesses, wasting subprocess startup overhead; static golden fixtures with fast version-drift assertions plus a bounded representative live contract preserve coverage while eliminating redundant execution.

AST provenance fixture setup consumes 46-51 seconds by rediscovering caller/parent relationships for every test; caching indices once per process preserves all 24 contracted verdict tuples and guards while reducing setup wall time.

Complexity lock runs the same OS/Python-invariant policy 4 times across Ubuntu and macOS matrix cells instead of once, wasting ~154 runner-seconds; moving it to the lint job eliminates duplication without reducing coverage.

Editor fixture setup (socket.getfqdn call) consistently exceeds 30 seconds on macOS, and Gerrit 1792's cancellation fix plus static Pandoc corpus relocation to External Integration removed predecessor admission delays, but post-remediation runs remain 88 seconds above the 30-minute target on average, requiring further investigation of distributed test throughput rather than single long poles.
